input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Paragraph (h) gives AP the assignment freedom we want (affiliate, asset purchaser and merger successor without consent, with a reasonableness standard on other consents), but it makes that carve-out mutual, so Kubient can move the Agreement to any affiliate or successor without our consent and with no bar on assignment to an AP competitor. Because the retained no-consent affiliate exception for Kubient is inconsistent with the fallback level (other assignments require consent) and we will not cure that by giving up AP's own carve-out, we target the preferred position: the carve-out becomes AP-only, Kubient's assignments remain consent-gated (consent not unreasonably withheld, already present), Kubient may not assign to an AP competitor, and we confirm expressly that an AP change of control gives Kubient no termination right (the termination clause in paragraph 4 contains no change-of-control trigger today).

proposal.summary: Make the no-consent assignment carve-out Customer-only, bar Kubient from assigning to our competitors, and confirm no Kubient termination right on our change of control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have limited the no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out to AP so that Kubient still needs our consent (not unreasonably withheld) to assign, added a bar on assignment to an AP competitor, and confirmed that a change of control of AP gives Kubient no termination right.
